title: Probabilistic grace-window allocator for KV-aware continuous batching
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce a probabilistic grace-window allocator that allows short, bounded non-preemptible windows for ongoing in-flight model slices while accounting for KV cache residency and overall GPU memory pressure. The goal is to reduce harmful tail latency spikes for best-effort tenants while preserving SLOs for high-tier customers and avoiding heavy KV churn during frequent preemptions.
acceptance_criteria: New allocator can be toggled per-node and per-cluster via runtime flag
P99 latency for P2 workload under mixed load improves by >= 12% compared to current preemptor baseline in the regression harness
Observed KV cache eviction churn (evictions per minute) decreases by >= 20% for medium-length requests (512-1k tokens) in stress tests
No regression in P50/P95 for P0 tenants (> -5%) and no increased OOMs during 2-hour soak
Ship a runtime config and docs page explaining knob semantics and expected trade-offs
tasks: Design: finalize probabilistic grace-window distribution and parameters (Ava + Diego)
Prototype: implement grace window sampling in continuous batcher (ENG runtime)
KV accounting: extend residency metrics to attribute windows to tenant slices
Preemption integration: modify preemptor to consult grace window before interrupting a slice
Memory safety: add guard to avoid granting windows that cause node GPU reservation > 95%
Tests: unit tests for sampler, e2e regression harness against baseline
Perf: run mixed-tenant stress jobs and collect latency + eviction metrics
Docs: runtime flag docs, rollout guidance, and ops playbook
Rollout: canary on 5% of nodes then 25% then full cluster with automated rollback on SLO breach
design_notes: Motivation: Frequent preemptions lead to KV cache thrash because short-lived slices get interrupted and their KV context is evicted/invalidated. Allowing a small probabilistic grace period reduces churn and amortizes KV costs.

Approach: On batch admission, sample a grace-window length from an exponential-mixture distribution: mostly 0 (no grace) with a light tail that grants 10-50ms windows ~5-15% of the time; parameters are tenant-weighted by tier and request size.
KV accounting: Tag sampled windows into slice metadata and treat the window as reserved for KV residency accounting so the preemptor prefers evicting slices without active windows.
Safety: Cap combined reserved windows to a node-level budget computed from free GPU memory and a conservative KV-residency multiplier to avoid overcommit.
Fairness: To avoid starvation, use a decaying credit per tenant that increases probability of receiving a window if the tenant was recently preempted, bounded by SLA tier.

Alternative considered: deterministic short quanta allocation (round-robin) — rejected because it increased median latency for latency-sensitive tenants and required global synchronization across shards.
Telemetry: New metrics: grace_window_granted_count, grace_window_ms_histogram, grace_window_eviction_savings_estimate, kv_evictions_by_window_tag
implementation_notes: Files touched: runtime/batcher/admit.cpp, runtime/preemptor/preemptor.cpp, runtime/kv/accounting.cpp, metrics/registry.cpp
Sampler API: provide Sampler::sampleGraceWindow(tenant_id, request_size, tier) returns int ms
Admission path: when a batch becomes in-flight, annotate slice metadata with 'grace_window_ms' and set a small timer to clear it
Preemptor change: check slice.metadata.grace_window_ms > now ? skip_preempt : allow_preempt
Node budget: compute node_guard = floor(available_gpu_memory * kv_window_fraction / typical_kv_residency) to cap total concurrent windows
Backward compatibility: default flags disabled. When enabled default params conservative: base_prob=0.06, tail_lambda=0.006, max_concurrent_windows_per_node=40
Performance notes: sampling must be fast and lock-free in hot path; precompute per-tenant RNG seeds and do single-instruction sampling when possible
Safety tests: fuzz preemption under synthetic workload that stresses KV and mem asynchronously to check caps
perf_targets: Under mixed synthetic workload (70% best-effort, 30% P0): P99 latency for best-effort improves >= 12%
Total KV evictions per node drops >= 20% on 1 hour stress run
No more than 0.2% increase in P0 P99 latency
Memory overhead for tracking windows < 0.5% of node GPU memory
test_plan: Unit tests for sampler edge cases (zero prob, cap enforcement)
Integration: run regression harness comparing baseline preemptor to new allocator across request length buckets (<=256, 512-1k, >1k)
Chaos: introduce synthetic node memory pressure and verify allocator respects max_concurrent_windows_per_node
Soak: 2-hour soak on canary cluster with production-like traffic mix and continuous KV eviction monitoring
A/B: launch 10% of traffic to nodes with feature on and compare SLO deltas over 48h
rollout_plan: Feature gated: default OFF in stable; enable via runtime flag for canary nodes
Phase 1: Canary (5 nodes) for 24 hours with strict alerts on P0 SLO delta > 1%
Phase 2: 25% node rollout for 72 hours, check KV eviction metric and tail latency trends
Phase 3: full cluster rollout with monitoring dashboard and 4-hour rollback window if automated SLO monitors trip
Fallback: toggle runtime.flag.prob_grace_enabled = false and drain existing windows quickly by setting base_prob=0
